subject.title: fix(sessions): prune every counted archive class before evicting searchable history

question: Should the default SQLite hard-disk-budget path be allowed to delete manual-compaction and legacy store backup archives in order to preserve searchable historical sessions?
rationale: Both outcomes are irreversible under disk pressure: the current behavior can evict searchable session history, while this PR can remove recovery copies. Source evidence establishes the implementation choice, but not which retained artifact class is the intended product priority.

options.title: Prefer searchable history
options.body: Approve pruning counted `.bak` archives before historical session eviction, retaining the PR’s documented default hard-budget order.

options.title: Prefer backup retention
options.body: Keep compaction and legacy backups out of hard-budget deletion and define a separate accounting or operator-managed retention policy.

recommendation.title: Prefer searchable history
recommendation.body: Approve pruning counted `.bak` archives before historical session eviction, retaining the PR’s documented default hard-budget order.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged predecessor established the adjacent archive-retention/accounting boundary this PR extends.
